52. Chapter on the Propagation and Protection of the Dharma Master. *Mahādharmolkā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, Chapter Fifty-two: The Propagation and Protection of the Dharma Master.
Ānanda, at that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Emitting Light addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
Kauśika, do you understand these skillful means and parables that I have spoken?
Kauśika, for this reason you should first understand that these words refer to fourteen bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Why is this?
Because they were previously born among these gods.
For what reason did they make such a vow?
It was to demonstrate that they were free from indolence.
By this cause and condition, upon casting off their bodies, they were immediately reborn in the palace of the asuras.
For this reason, they cannot understand even a small portion of it,
let alone be able to hear and receive these three teachings of the Treasury of Karma.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
"Now, you have long resided upon this mountain peak in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven;
are you able to know how many beings there are dwelling here among this immeasurable and boundless great assembly?"
Furthermore, one is able to know how many years, according to human reckoning, these beings have resided there;
and one also knows the extent of their celestial clothing, food, drink, and all such matters.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
"World-Honored One,
I have already fully understood."
The Buddha said,
"Kauśika, if someone comes and asks..."
"Now, for this great assembly, how much labor is required for the preparation of the food and the necessary utensils? He asked this;
how would you answer?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:
"World-Honored One,
I have nothing to report."
For what reason?
World-Honored One,
whatever clothing, food, and various requisites are required here in our realm of the Thirty-three Gods, [all are provided].
Because mindfulness arises spontaneously and is not a product of deliberate effort,
the Buddha said: "Kauśika!"
All phenomena are likewise thus;
they all abide within the mind, and at the very moment one contemplates them, they are accomplished. Kausika!
Just as sentient beings born from eggs are conceived merely through the thought of the mind,
so too it is with all phenomena.
Kauśika, it is all due to mental intention that phenomena immediately manifest before one.
Furthermore, it is like all classes of moisture-born beings, such as fish, turtles, crocodiles, dragons, *ḍimbi*, and *mīna*.
All of these are included among those born from eggs.
They travel either one yojana,
or two yojanas, or as far as three or four.
Or again, it may exceed seven days;
having reached that stage, he settles himself within the egg so as not to cause exhaustion,
and thus brings it to maturity.
Kauśika, these three collections of teachings are likewise:
whenever they are recollected, those karmas manifest before one.
One should further understand that [the teaching] proceeds in successive order without confusion,
continues in an uninterrupted succession, and is in harmony and correspondence with the meaning of those phrases.
For what reason have I taught the gateway of the letter A for you?
It is because it is explained by means of the analogy of a wooden board.
As for the gateway of the letter Ka:
Because it is taught by means of letters.
As for the letter-gateway "Na," it is because it is taught by means of the equality of letters, syllables, and phrases.
When it is spoken in this way, you should all uphold it together;
there is no further dharma that may be omitted.
However, you must know that these forty-two phrases are inscribed upon wooden tablets.
Having understood this,
those Dharma masters, while seated upon the Dharma throne in the midst of the great assembly, were about to preach.
Within these three dharma-gates,
the Dharma Master should first bring the visualization of the syllable *A* to mind and maintain it in continuous succession;
once this has been brought into harmony, [the practice proceeds].
One should then proclaim forty-two phrases;
by such analysis, one obtains two hundred phrases,
which in turn yield ten phrases.
Just as the five constituent parts of a lute must be harmonized to produce the five notes,
so too that Dharma teacher, having harmonized these five notes with his retinue of five members, [proceeds].
Having perfected the one hundred phrases of vocal resonance,
they are able to discern and know them accordingly; thus,
all written characters and recitations manifest before them.
Having thus attained the state of continuous manifestation and maintained it,
just as one attains the complete production of phonemes and phrases through vocal sound,
so too can one preach therein such that no other sound can be produced.
That Dharma Master gives rise to the five tones and phrases according to the Dharma.
When the Dharma Master analyzes the phrase of the letter "A," he accomplishes the activity of emptiness through great eloquence.
He cuts through the doubts of thousands of sentient beings;
when questioned, he is never hurried or flustered,
but calmly provides explanations through parables.
Having first explained the hundreds of doctrinal gateways within the great palace,
he interpreted them in such a way that the entire assembly was filled with joy,
just like the great congregation gathered by the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
It is likewise for him:
having attained the mastery of the faculties and skillful wisdom,
he teaches in this manner for the sake of all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
you should with single-minded devotion believe in and accept this Dharma—
the place where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha employs vocal discourse, skillful means, and parables for its explanation.
How should one reflect? One should reflect that it must take six years.
Having formed this reflection, one should enter meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and practice in accordance with the Dharma as it has been taught.
Having already engaged in this practice, he no longer indulged in negligence;
with single-mindedness and right mindfulness, he applied analytical reflection in accord with this intention.
Only after six years did he attain complete and perfect fulfillment.
Just as with the letter-gateway Na, one also practices various forms of mindfulness for six years until they are perfectly fulfilled.
Having cultivated such mindfulness, one immediately attains the realization and knowledge of all distinctions among vocal sounds.
Kauśika, if these three gateways of phrases are well maintained,
no one will be able to know their limits, Kauśika.
It is impossible that any of the skillful means, parables, or explanatory gateways of meaning spoken by the Buddhas,
the Tathāgatas, could be false. Kausika,
it is like a farmer who is skilled at managing his cultivation.
At another time, he gathered a multitude of farmers and addressed them, saying:
"All of you people should speak these words."
"From this day forward, now that we have sown the seeds, we pray that they do not sprout and do not ripen into fruit.
Then those farmers all said to one another, "Alas!
We now pray for your seeds!"
Neither arising nor forming, and likewise free from indolence. Kauśika,
what do you think?
"Once those seeds have been well cultivated, do they attain non-arising?
No, World-Honored One.
Do they attain non-formation?"
"No, World-Honored One.
Kauśika, these three Dharma-gates are likewise so."
The infinite gateways of meaning born of space contain the complete names and sequences of all phenomena;
even if they were to remain hidden and unmanifest for immeasurable periods of time.
It is impossible that they would ever perish.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
whether it be toward a son of good family or toward a Tathāgata, all sentient beings—
Those sentient beings who hear this sūtra dharma-gate,
whether by reciting it, explaining it, practicing it in successive stages, or instructing others in its transmission, will,
when questioned or challenged regarding this gateway of wisdom, [be able to respond].
It is neither subject to subjugation nor characterized by silence.
Why is this? Because these activities of wisdom are immeasurable and boundless.
That instructor is able to cause all those immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who have never heard [this teaching] to fully analyze and achieve eloquence.
Furthermore, because one has achieved mastery oneself,
when someone comes to inquire about the meaning of this Dharma,
one is able to elucidate and analyze the points of that inquiry.
Having explained it in this way and answered with such arguments,
he further thought to himself:
"If someone were to come and ask me about this matter..."
I shall continue to provide explanations for them.
If there are those who pose questions based upon the Tathāgata’s teaching,
I shall analyze and explain all their points of doubt.
Furthermore, it is for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings of the future.
If there are those who can keep this dharma-gate in mind,
or study it from time to time.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
you should know that such a person who practices in this way will achieve accomplishment before long.
Within this Dharma, it is not only those sentient beings who are unfit vessels that fail to give rise to faith in the Buddha's teachings;
there may also be sentient beings who, though possessing faith, [do not practice].
Furthermore, Kauśika, if they are unable to practice in accordance with the teaching,
it is not only that there will be no teachers of the Dharma in the world, but the Dharma itself will utterly perish.
If there are no people who listen to the Dharma or inquire about it,
you should know that at such a time the Dharma will not endure for long. Why is this?
In this world, there are no questioners because there is no practice or study.
Because there is no practice or study, one cannot know;
since one cannot know, how can one practice and uphold [the teaching]?
Because they are unable to practice it, the world is entirely blind and dark, lacking a guide who knows the way.
Thus, in such ignorance, who would establish the Dharma?

If there were no Dharma, then in this world there would be no filial support for parents, no reverence for elders or affection for the young, no distinction between the old and the young or the noble and the humble, and no performance of duties, consolations, or words of praise and commendation.
"All worldly affairs are exhausted; who could be their creator?
Kauśika, if a person does not understand the nature of worldly phenomena..."
How could one possibly analyze and explain the meanings of worldly affairs?
Since they neither understand nor can practice them,
even basic worldly goodness does not exist.
"How can one learn the wisdom of all Buddhas?
For this reason, one must not cease from worldly affairs.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
When any Dharma masters wish to preach,
they must adorn the place of teaching with four kinds of ornaments.
What are these four?
Kauśika, at that time, the Dharma-preacher should first select such a location.
That place is vast and spacious, with level and even terrain;
it is free from elevations and depressions, tiles, stones, gravel, pebbles, thorns, and wicked brambles.
Furthermore, there are no foul weeds, nor mosquitoes, gadflies, snakes, scorpions, or any other venomous insects.
The ground there was level, beautiful, soft, supple, and exquisite.
It abounded in gardens, ponds, flowers, fruits, and groves of trees;
the place was pure and far removed from clamor and distraction.
In summer there was no intense heat, and in winter there was no extreme cold.
The fourfold assembly lived together in mutual harmony and peace.
Both the Dharma Master and his listeners experienced complete joy and contentment.
Kauśika, this is the first way in which that Dharma-preacher adorns the place where he teaches.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
When any Dharma masters wish to preach,
there shall be protectors of the Dharma in that region,
as well as those who listen to the Dharma.
Out of reverence for the Dharma, one should provide for the Dharma-preacher a decorated and spacious Dharma-seat,
and prepare many kinds of excellent, exquisite mats and soft bedding.
All items required for the lecture were placed upon the seat;
as the assembly gazed upon them, their reverence for the Dharma increased,
and the Dharma Master sat there in tranquility, preaching the teaching.
Kauśika, this is the second way in which that Dharma-preacher adorns the place where he teaches.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
When any Dharma masters are about to preach the Dharma,
those who protect the Dharma and those who listen to it,
out of reverence for the Dharma, should with sincere mind, diligence, and valor guard the Dharma masters so that those evil sentient beings may not destroy, slander, or obstruct the True Dharma.
"Furthermore, Kausika, do not allow men, women, boys, or girls to come and go in a noisy and distracting manner, thereby hindering and confusing the Dharma-preacher. Kausika,
this is the third way to adorn the preaching site for that Dharma-preacher."
Furthermore, Kauśika,
when those Dharma-preachers are correctly expounding the teaching,

those who protect the Dharma and the assembly of listeners, out of reverence for the Dharma, should select five, ten, or many persons who are respectful, knowledgeable of the Dharma, and capable of remaining behind the Dharma-preacher.
Observe the great assembly so as not to allow interference or disorder.
First, grasp the intent of the Dharma Master’s instructions and,
acting in accordance with the Dharma, rectify the community.
If at any time there is a person whose speech causes confusion among the assembly,
one must immediately question them regarding the source of their words and prohibit them in accordance with the Dharma.
If anyone should engage in frivolous laughter or act with improper conduct,
they should immediately be interrogated and rebuked so that such behavior is severed.
One must constantly ensure that the great assembly remains tranquil, their faculties restrained and pure, abiding in body and speech according to the teachings.
However, when those people observe the assembly,
their conduct must be careful and deliberate, not hasty or precipitate;
they should employ kind speech and refrain from uttering harsh words.
Whenever you speak, do so only to ensure that those before you understand and comprehend;
you must then remain silent.
You should not speak loudly or raise your voice to draw attention and cause others to take notice.
Why is this? Because one does not wish to cause others to encounter obstacles to the Dharma for the sake of many sentient beings due to other matters. Kausika.
This is the fourth way to adorn the place where that Dharma-preacher speaks.

If one can adorn the location of the Dharma-exposition with these four matters, it will ensure that the sūtras spoken by that Dharma-preacher encounter no obstacles and will ultimately circulate widely.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
when those Dharma-preachers are about to speak,
they should first observe that assembly.
What are their inclinations and what teachings do they require?
Just as those various desires are fulfilled according to the time,
may all sentient beings bring their roots of virtue to completion.
It also causes the growth of eloquence and skill in speech,
making it unimpeded and pure in all circumstances,
so that wise persons may easily understand and comprehend it.
It is observable and verifiable, free from defilement;
far removed from the hindrances and entanglements, the body, speech, and all faculties are entirely tranquil;
and the contemplation of samādhi continues in an uninterrupted succession.
If a person, having heard and understood the Dharma from a Dharma-master,
practices it throughout the long night and never abandons the treasury of the three types of teaching and practice.
They will attain unimpeded mastery over all written characters and verbal expressions.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
whenever these Dharma-preachers expound the Dharma, [they shall be endowed with such qualities].
One should make a vow to accomplish this gateway of meaning and act as a refuge for all sentient beings.
Once the Dharma Master has awakened to such meanings, [he should proceed].
Furthermore, one should reflect in this way:
"Now that I have awakened to such a Dharma-gate,
how may I ensure that my verbal karma becomes excellent?"
The speech they utter is pure and discerning, free from turbidity;
it is not a disruptive sound nor does it have the resonance of lamentation.
They constantly attain subtle and uninterrupted eloquence.
It is solely for the purpose of revealing and manifesting the meaning of this sūtra’s dharma-gate that,
when that Dharma-preacher speaks in such a manner,
there is none who does not know it and none who does not understand it.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
when a Dharma-preacher wishes to preach the Dharma and the assembly has already gathered,
The Dharma Master should first contemplate the immeasurable characteristics of that great assembly with three kinds of mind.
What kind of sentient beings are clever and of sharp intelligence?
By contemplating in this way with these three minds, [he should proceed].
Alternatively, through supernormal knowledge, he may perceive that within the assembly there are those possessing such characteristics;
in that case, the Dharma teacher should first proclaim for that great multitude matters such as the merits of giving.
When this was spoken, many sentient beings read,
recited, received, upheld, and joyfully practiced it; meanwhile,
that Dharma teacher continuously elucidated these gateways of meaning— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— without interruption.
When the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas teach this Dharma,
they are able to manifest such characteristics of pure meaning through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of gateways.
At that time, the Dharma Master again explained this meaning:
"One must never abandon the Tathāgata’s treasury of the Dharma;
one should mindfully maintain and uphold the Dharma-gate of the letter A."
The initial verbal discourse is established for others in an uninterrupted succession;
the dharma-gate of the letter *ka* is taught next in succession,
and the dharma-gate of the letter *na* is the final culmination.
Having reflected thus,
the eloquence of the Tathāgata will manifest before you of its own accord;
regarding these words, you should further become skillful in means and firm.
Once firmly established, this mass of wisdom is spontaneously accomplished;
like Mount Sumeru, it cannot be destroyed,
and no heterodox practitioners can cause it to waver.
No teacher of any treatise is able to overturn or uproot them.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
when these Dharma-preachers are expounding the Dharma, [they shall be protected].
One should rouse great diligence with heroic vigor;
once the faculties are clear and all matters are fully accomplished,
one should then extensively proclaim such teachings as these various aggregates for the fourfold assembly of that world.
Because they skillfully know the various characteristics of each [phenomenon],
once they have awakened to this knowledge, they maintain constant mindfulness before them,
providing immeasurable eloquence in analysis and explanation.
How is it known that the five aggregates (skandhas) and so forth are a collection?
For what reason are those collections of aggregates called "aggregates" (skandha)?
Furthermore, by what characteristic are the collections of aggregates properly understood?
Having skillfully explained these aggregates of the skandhas,
one should then proceed to proclaim, in successive order, the gateway to the signlessness of all phenomena for entry into reality, Kausika.
I have already explained the meaning of the summary of the characteristics of these four great elements.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
at that time the Dharma-preacher should speak as follows:
If there were any collection of forms therein,
what further acceptance or abiding could there be in that,
such that one could say there is such an acceptance of forms?
Previously, such sutras already existed and should now be brought before them;
furthermore, there are people who constantly and continuously explain such doctrinal gateways for others.
How does one teach such a Dharma in continuous succession?
It is by teaching in accordance with how those sentient beings give rise to joy and delight, desiring to hear it;
and by teaching in accordance with how those sentient beings remain single-mindedly focused on the Dharma, free from further distracted thoughts.
Just as those sentient beings possess the vessel for receiving the Dharma;
just as those sentient beings are capable of being brought to maturity;
just as those sentient beings, having heard the Dharma, possess a sense of shame and remorse.
Just as those sentient beings are able to hear and receive such a sūtra,
according to its sequence, according to the sūtra itself,
according to its power, and according to their conceptual discrimination.
Thus it should be upheld.
And among that assembly, there was not a single person who gave rise to a mind of regression or failed to listen to the Dharma, Kauśika.
Those Dharma masters should accomplish the ritual matters in this manner;
all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, have spoken thus.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
When those Dharma masters preach the Dharma,
they must manifest extraordinary and marvelous matters.
Suppose there were someone from this village or perhaps from another village.
Or again, having arrived from a city, a town, or another region,
they ask about such matters of Dharma and say to the Dharma Master:
"How can what I have now asked be understood?
However, that Dharma Master should first contemplate this meaning until it becomes thoroughly proficient,
so that he may be able to skillfully explain it through expedient means in response to any question."
Being free from fear and without delay,
they satisfy all that is asked.
Such is the case when this Dharma teacher preaches the Dharma.
Do not speak of matters that cause distraction to others;
by this cause and condition, you shall obtain great benefit.
And as for those sentient beings who listen to it there—
They all gave rise to joy and constantly came to listen to the Dharma.
Kauśika, it is for this reason.
At that time, that Dharma-preacher should universally expound it to accomplish great benefit.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
those Dharma-preachers who are able to penetrate such a Dharma as this—
Although they may not be able to expound the *bodhi* of all Buddhas when preaching the Dharma,
they are nonetheless able to make the meaning of this teaching clear;
they skillfully understand expedient means and possess a broad and comprehensive mastery.
He also preaches it for others who listen and receive it at the proper time.
Once such a Dharma teacher has thus attained thorough mastery,
if there should be someone who comes to listen at an improper time or comes to question with improper words, [he remains unperturbed].
One should immediately provide instruction.
If there are members of the fourfold assembly— monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— or other sentient beings,
one must not fail to speak for them at the improper time or with inappropriate words.
Thereafter, they no longer came to listen.
Because they did not listen, they were unable to propagate the essential points of the Dharma for others or to reveal them to sentient beings. Kauśika.
For these reasons,
this Dharma-gate cannot be fully revealed.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
If these Dharma masters do not dwell with a correct mind regarding this teaching but give rise to false reflections,
then because of those false reflections they fall into wrong views.
Thus, due to their erroneous discrimination, such Dharma masters are unable to comprehend the meaning of that sūtra.
Thus, dwelling within a mass of ignorance and nescience,
and because that Dharma teacher abides in wrong views, all the celestial deities from times past will simultaneously abandon him and no longer provide protection.
Because they are not protected by the devas,
they lack majesty, power, and radiance;
and because they lack such power, all their actions do not conform to the Vinaya.
All other roots of goodness will utterly diminish.

Thus, even those listeners who previously had the Dharma master constantly explain the meanings of the sūtras and other teachings for them will now slander him, reject his words, and refuse to accept them.
How much more so, Kauśika, for one who does not act in accordance with the precepts and yet comes again to listen to their exposition?
If there are people in the world who lack faith and practice,
even their own wives, children, and kinsmen will not obey them;
how much less would a great assembly come to listen to them?
Furthermore, Kauśika,
such a Dharma-preacher lacks the factor of faith,
namely: "The Tathāgata always says that one does not rely on the precepts and does not act according to the teachings."
Kauśika, because these Dharma-preachers lack the element of faith,
they cannot be said to possess roots of goodness.
When evil increases, one will inevitably undergo its retribution.
If the Tathāgatas were to describe such retribution as it truly is,
that person, upon hearing it, would vomit much hot blood from their mouth.
Because of this affliction, one shall meet their end.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—
Desiring to cause all sentient beings in the world to awaken to and understand all phenomena,
those deluded people give rise to a mind of jealousy toward these teachings.
Yet, they were ultimately unable to think in this way:
"If I were to be stingy with the Dharma and keep it secret without teaching it,
then because of such parsimony, the Dharma would gradually become difficult to obtain or even disappear."
If I do not speak, how can those who listen to the Dharma hear it as it was spoken and receive it as it was heard?
Since there would be no hearing or receiving, how could they practice it?
If it were thus, one would cause immeasurable sentient beings not to know this Dharma.
How, then, could they develop a sense of rare wonder toward the Dharma?
For these reasons, [one should not speak of it].
I should not now act with stinginess toward these teachings among all sentient beings.
Kauśika, such a person can never be established as a witness within the Buddha-dharma.
Kauśika, you should regard such deluded people as those who wish to set their own price for the priceless, true jewel of the Dharma.
Kauśika, you should further know this:
such deluded people wish to establish various marks within the markless Dharma of the Tathāgata’s threefold treasury of karma.
"Kauśika, this is also a point where the Dharma-preacher lacks faith.
The Tathāgata has thus explained it through such skillful means."
Furthermore, Kauśika,
if there is a Dharma-preacher who is skillful in grasping the meaning within such sūtras and abides in right mindfulness.
By means of various skillful expedients, you shall open and exalt the gates of the Dharma,
bringing great benefit to all the worlds;
at that time, you should observe this well.
Wherever there are beautiful gardens,
one should cause those sentient beings to cultivate, maintain, and adorn them with many kinds of trees, flowers, and fruits, including all their various forms and names.
Even if one were to smear a single lump of cow dung over the ground of the grove where the trees grow,
once it has been thus adorned,
one should then invite the Dharma Master to deliver a discourse.
And when that Dharma master was preaching the Dharma,
there were forest-dwelling devas, earth devas, tree devas,
and all the devas belonging to the higher realms within the grove.
All the gandharvas, kinnaras, garuḍas, mahoragas, nāgas, and yakṣas—
these various classes of beings informed one another,
joyfully praising that adorned person.
He was able to smear the area beneath the grove with cow dung,
guarding it with mindfulness without ever forgetting for even a moment,
and he respectfully circumambulated that grove as if serving a stupa or temple.
Kauśika, if that Dharma-preacher, for the sake of not severing the Dharma for the world at large,
should depart from this place and wish to go to another region.
At that time, the devas and spirits who protect this forest will continue to offer constant worship to such a forest on this ground.
Furthermore, Kauśika:
If there is a Dharma master who practices in this manner,
that person shall obtain an immeasurable accumulation of merit;
all that they speak will be received and upheld by others.
Why is this? Because that Dharma teacher practices the Buddha’s teachings, accords with the Dharma gates, never deviates from them, and never severs the gateway of the meaning of the Dharma. Kausika!
For these reasons, those who act as Dharma-preachers should first apply themselves with diligence within this Dharma and only then teach others.
If one does not exert oneself, who will believe them?
Kauśika, for this reason,
that Dharma-preacher should skillfully enter such a Dharma-gate.
Because profound wisdom and skillful means reveal and manifest the treasury of the Dharma;
because through non-negligence one can attain great power;
and because through skillful means one knows with certainty that retribution will not be received.
Because it accomplishes the karmic fruit of the mind through the gathering of compassion;
because it enables all sentient beings to know the proper seasons;
and because it reaches skillful wisdom while remaining unmoved from the true state.
At that time, once that Dharma-master has attained this,
he must first understand the distinctions among the roots of goodness, skillful means, wisdom, and conduct of sentient beings before preaching the Dharma.
When the Dharma-master abides in these skillful means and preaches from the treasury of the Dharma, [he shall succeed].
One shall thereby obtain an immeasurable and peerless mass of great merit,
as well as such an immeasurable and boundless mass of great wisdom;
one should then abide within this mass of great generosity and right knowledge.
Moreover, that Dharma Master has reached the further shore of immeasurable diligence;
for the sake of all sentient beings, he causes them likewise to abide in the wisdom of skillful means that universally gathers others through compassion and loving-kindness.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra,
the deva Subhūti, the Venerable Ānanda,
and all the devas, humans, asuras, and others—
The entire assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
received it upon the crowns of their heads and practiced accordingly. *Mahādharmolkā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, Fascicle Twenty.
